A pre-run modifier shapes what *runs*. A **result visitor** shapes what you do
with the *results* — the `output.xml` a run produces. It is a `ResultVisitor`:
Robot Framework walks the finished suites and tests and calls your methods, so
you can build a custom report, compute metrics, or export data.

Because results live in `output.xml`, you can process them **after** the run,
with `rebot`, without re-running anything — reporting is decoupled from
execution.

```diagram
tree "A result visitor walks the results"
output.xml #doc -- saved after the run {
  Suite -- end_suite fires per suite {
    Test -- visit_test fires per finished test
  }
}
note "Processed after the run with rebot, decoupled from execution"
```

## Task 1 — Turn results into a markdown report

**Goal:** create `ext/ResultReport.py` — a `ResultVisitor` that collects each
finished test and, at the end of the top suite, writes `results/rebot_report.md`
as a markdown table.

Here is the same base class with a different job — recording only the failures.
Adapt it to collect every test into a table.

<!-- example -->
```python
import pathlib
from robot.api import ResultVisitor


class FailReport(ResultVisitor):
    def __init__(self):
        self.failed = []

    def visit_test(self, test):
        if test.status == "FAIL":
            self.failed.append(test.name)

    def end_suite(self, suite):
        if suite.parent is not None:
            return
        pathlib.Path("results").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        pathlib.Path("results/failures.txt").write_text("\n".join(self.failed) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
```
<!-- /example -->

**Check:** `ext/ResultReport.py` defines a `ResultVisitor`.

<!-- hint -->
Collect rows as you visit: `def visit_test(self, test):` appends
`(test.name, test.status)` to `self.rows`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
Write once, at the top suite. `end_suite` fires for every suite, so guard on the
root: `if suite.parent is not None: return`, then build the table and
`write_text` it to `results/rebot_report.md`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- solution -->
```python
import pathlib
from robot.api import ResultVisitor


class ResultReport(ResultVisitor):
    def __init__(self):
        self.rows = []

    def visit_test(self, test):
        self.rows.append((test.name, test.status))

    def end_suite(self, suite):
        if suite.parent is not None:
            return
        lines = ["| Test | Status |", "| --- | --- |"]
        lines += [f"| {name} | {status} |" for name, status in self.rows]
        pathlib.Path("results").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        pathlib.Path("results/rebot_report.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
```
<!-- /solution -->

## Task 2 — Reprocess the saved results

Run the suite once to produce `output.xml`, then build your report from it with
`rebot` — no tests re-run:

```bash
uv run robot --outputdir results checks/orders.robot
uv run rebot --prerebotmodifier ext/ResultReport.py results/output.xml
```

**Check:** `results/rebot_report.md` is a table built from the saved results.
